title: A Beautiful Life
slides:
1.
Each day I'll do a gold-en deed,
By helping those who are in need;
My life on earth is but a span,
And so I'll do the best I can,
the best I can.
1 - A Beautiful Life
Words and Music by: William M. Golden
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

1 - A Beautiful Life
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

Life's evening sun is sinking low,
A few more days and I must go,
To meet the deeds that I have done
Where there will be no set-ting sun.
c - A Beautiful Life
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

c - A Beautiful Life
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2.
To be a child of God each day,
My light must shine along the way;
I'll sing His praise while ages roll,
And strive to help some troubled soul,
some troubled soul.
2 - A Beautiful Life
Words and Music by: William M. Golden
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2 - A Beautiful Life
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

Life's evening sun is sinking low,
A few more days and I must go,
To meet the deeds that I have done
Where there will be no set-ting sun.
c - A Beautiful Life
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

c - A Beautiful Life
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3.
The only life that will endure,
Is one that's kind and good and pure;
And so for God I'll take my stand,
Each day I'll lend a helping hand,
a helping hand.
3 - A Beautiful Life
Words and Music by: William M. Golden
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3 - A Beautiful Life
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

Life's evening sun is sinking low,
A few more days and I must go,
To meet the deeds that I have done
Where there will be no set-ting sun.

© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

c - A Beautiful Life
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4.
I'll help some one in time of need,
And journey on with rapid speed;
I'll help the sick and poor and weak,
And words of kindness to them speak,
kind words I'll speak.

© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4 - A Beautiful Life
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

To meet the deeds that I have done
Where there will be no set-ting sun.

title: A Beautiful Prayer
slides:
1.
In the Bible we read of a beautiful prayer,
A prayer sent to heaven above;
It was prayed by a heart that was laden with care
And filled with such wonderful love.

He said, "loving Father,
If you will let this cup pass from me;"

Of the anguish death would bring to His own,
How was deep was His sorrow
When Jesus was praying alone.

title: A Charge To Keep I Have
slides:
1.
A charge to keep I have,
A God to glorify;
A never dying soul to save,
And fit it for the sky.
1 - A Charge to Keep I Have
Words by: Charles Wesley
Music by: Lowell Mason
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2.
To serve the present age,
My calling to fulfill
O may it all my powers engage
To do my Master's will!
2 - A Charge to Keep I Have
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™
Words by: Charles Wesley
Music by: Lowell Mason

3.
Arm me with jealous care,
As in Thy sight to live,
And O, thy servant, Lord, prepare,
A strict account to give!
3 - A Charge to Keep I Have
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™
Words by: Charles Wesley
Music by: Lowell Mason

4.
Help me to watch and pray,
And on Thyself rely,
Assured if I my trust betray,
I shall forever die.
4 - A Charge to Keep I Have
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™
Words by: Charles Wesley
Music by: Lowell Mason

title: A Mighty Fortress
slides:
1.
A mighty fortress is our God,
A bulwark never failing;
Our helper He, amid the flood
Of mortal ills prevailing.
For still our ancient foe
Doth seek to work us woe;
His craft and power are great,
And, armed with cruel hate,
On earth is not his equal.
1 - A Mighty Fortress
Words and Music by: Martin Luther
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

1 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

1 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

1 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2.
Did we in our own strength confide
Our striving would be losing;
Were not the right One on our side
The Man of God's own choosing.
Dost ask who that may be?
Christ Jesus, it is He;
Lord Sabaoth is His name,
From age to age the same,
And He must win the battle.
2 - A Mighty Fortress
Words and Music by: Martin Luther
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3.
And though this world, with evil filled,
Should threaten to undo us;
We will not fear, for God hath willed
His truth to triumph thru us.
The prince of darkness grim -
We tremble not for him;
His rage we can endure,
For lo! his doom is sure:
One little word shall fell him.
3 - A Mighty Fortress
Words and Music by: Martin Luther
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4.
That word above all earthly powers -
No thanks to them - abideth;
The Spirit and the gifts are ours
Through Him who with us sideth.
Let goods and kindred go,
This mortal life also;
The body they may kill:
God's truth abideth still,
His kingdom is forever.
4 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4 - A Mighty Fortress
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

title: All Things Praise Thee
slides:
1.
All things praise Thee, Lord most high,
Heaven and earth, and sea and sky;
All were for Thy glory made,
That Thy greatness, thus displayed,
Should all worship bring to Thee;
All things praise Thee— Lord, may we!
1 - All Things Praise Thee
Words: George W. Conder
Music: Conrad Kocher / Arr.: William H. Monk
© 2006 The Paperless Hymnal®

2.
All things praise Thee— night to night
Sings in silent hymns of light;
All things praise Thee— day by day
Chants Thy power in burning ray;
Time and space are praising Thee;
All things praise Thee— Lord, may we!

Words: George W. Conder
Music: Conrad Kocher / Arr.: William H. Monk

All things praise Thee: heaven's high shrine
Rings with melody divine;
Lowly bending at Thy feet,
Seraph and archangel meet;
This their highest bliss, to be
Ever praising— Lord, may we!

title: Alleluia Sing To Jesus
slides:
1.
Alleluia! Sing to Jesus!
His the scepter, His the throne;
Alleluia! His the triumph,
His the victory a-lone.
Hark! The songs of peaceful Zion
Thunder like a mighty flood;
Jesus, out of every nation,
Has redeemed us by His blood.
1 - Alleluia! Sing to Jesus!
Words: William C. Dix
Music: Rowland H. Prichard / Arr.: Ralph Vaughan Williams
© 2006 The Paperless Hymnal®

1 - Alleluia! Sing to Jesus!

2.
Alleluia! Not as orphans
Are we left in sorrow now;
Alleluia! He is near us
Faith believes, nor questions how.
Through the cloud from sight received Him
When the forty days were o'er,
Shall our hearts forget His promise,
"I am with you evermore"?

Music: Rowland H. Prichard / Arr.: Ralph Vaughan Williams

Where the songs of all the sinless
Sweep across the crystal sea.

title: Am I A Soldier Of The Cross
slides:
1.
Am I a soldier of the cross,
A follower of the Lamb?
And shall I fear to own His cause,
Or blush to speak His name?
Must I be carried to the skies
On flowery beds of ease,
While others fought to win the prize,
And sailed through bloody seas?
1 - Am I A Soldier of the Cross?
Words by: Isaac Watts
Arr. By: R. M. M.
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

1 - Am I A Soldier of the Cross?
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2.
Are there no foes for me to face?
Must I not stem the flood?
Is this vile world a friend to grace,
To help me on to God?
Sure I must fight if I would reign:
Increase my courage, Lord;
I'll bear the toil, endure the pain,
Supported by Thy word.
2 - Am I A Soldier of the Cross?
Words by: Isaac Watts
Arr. By: R. M. M.
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2 - Am I A Soldier of the Cross?
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3.
Thy saints, in all this glorious war,
Shall conquer, though they die;
They see the triumph from afar
By faith's discerning eye.
When that illustrious day shall rise,
And all Thine armies shine
In robes of victory through the skies,
The glory shall be Thine.
3 - Am I A Soldier of the Cross?
Words by: Isaac Watts
Arr. By: R. M. M.
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3 - Am I A Soldier of the Cross?
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

title: Beneath The Cross Of Jesus
slides:
1.
Beneath the cross of Jesus
I fain would take my stand,
The shadow of a mighty rock
Within a weary land,
A home within the wilderness,
A rest upon the way,
From the burning of the noontide heat,
And the bur-den of the day.
1 – Beneath the Cross of Jesus
Words by: Elizabeth Clephane
Music by: Frederick C. Maker
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal®

1 – Beneath the Cross of Jesus
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal®

2.
O safe and happy shelter,
O refuge tried and sweet,
O trysting place where heaven's love
And heaven's justice meet!
As to the holy patriarch
That wondrous dream was given,
So seems my Savior's cross to me,
A ladder up to heaven.
2 – Beneath the Cross of Jesus
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal®
Words by: Elizabeth Clephane
Music by: Frederick C. Maker

2 – Beneath the Cross of Jesus
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal®

3.
Upon that cross of Jesus,
Mine eye at times can see
The very dying form of One
Who suffered there for me;
And from my smitten heart, with tears
Two wonders I confess;
The wonders of His glorious love,
And my own worth-less-ness.
3 – Beneath the Cross of Jesus
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal®
Words by: Elizabeth Clephane
Music by: Frederick C. Maker

3 – Beneath the Cross of Jesus
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal®

4.
I take, O cross, thy shadow
For my abiding place;
I ask no other sunshine than
The sunshine of His face;
Content to let the world go by,
To know no gain nor loss,
My sinful self my only shame,
My glory all the cross!
4 – Beneath the Cross of Jesus
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal®
Words by: Elizabeth Clephane
Music by: Frederick C. Maker

4 – Beneath the Cross of Jesus
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal®

title: Faith Is The Victory
slides:
1.
Encamped along the hills of light,
Ye Christian soldiers, rise,
And press the battle ere the night
Shall veil the glowing skies.
Against the foe in vales below
Let all our strength be hurled;
Faith is the victory, we know,
That overcomes the world.

Words by: John H. Yates
Music by: Ira D. Sankey
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

1 – Faith is the Victory
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

Faith is the victory!
Faith is the victory!
O glorious victory
That o-ver-comes the world.
c – Faith is the Victory
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2.
His banner over us is love,
Our sword the Word of God;
We tread the road the saints above
With shouts of triumph trod.
By faith they, like a whirlwind's breath,
Swept on o'er every field;
The faith by which they conquered death
Is still our shining shield.
2 – Faith is the Victory
Words by: John H. Yates
Music by: Ira D. Sankey
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2 – Faith is the Victory
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

Faith is the victory!
Faith is the victory!
O glorious victory
That o-ver-comes the world.
c – Faith is the Victory
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3.
On every hand the foe we find
Drawn up in dread array;
Let tents of ease be left behind,
And onward to the fray.
Salvation's helmet on each head,
With truth all girt about,
The earth shall tremble 'neath our tread,
And echo with our shout.
3 – Faith is the Victory
Words by: John H. Yates
Music by: Ira D. Sankey
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3 – Faith is the Victory
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

Faith is the victory!
Faith is the victory!
O glorious victory
That o-ver-comes the world.
c – Faith is the Victory
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4.
To him that overcomes the foe
White raiment shall be given;
Be-fore the angels he shall know
His name confessed in Heaven;
Then onward from the hills of light,
Our hearts with love aflame;
We'll vanquish all the hosts of night,
In Jesus' conquering name.

Words by: John H. Yates
Music by: Ira D. Sankey
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

How vast beyond all measure.

As wounds which mar the Chosen One
bring many sons to glory.

title: Jesus Lover Of My Soul Holbrook
slides: Jesus, Lover Of My Soul

title: Jesus Lover Of My Soul Holbrook
slides:
1.
Jesus, lover of my soul,
Let me to Thy bosom fly,
While the nearer waters roll,
While the tempest still is high;
Hide me, O my Savior, hide,
Till the storm of life is past;
Safe into the haven guide,
O receive my soul at last.
1 – Jesus, Lover of My Soul
Words: Charles Wesley
Music: Joseph P. Holbrook
© 2005 The Paperless Hymnal™

1 – Jesus, Lover of My Soul
© 2005 The Paperless Hymnal™

2.
Other refuge have I none,
Hangs my helpless soul on Thee;
Leave, O leave me not alone,
Still support and comfort me.
All my trust on Thee is stayed,
All my help from Thee I bring;
Cover my defenseless head
With the shadow of Thy wing.
2 – Jesus, Lover of My Soul
Words: Charles Wesley
Music: Joseph P. Holbrook
© 2005 The Paperless Hymnal™

2 – Jesus, Lover of My Soul
© 2005 The Paperless Hymnal™

3.
Thou, O Christ, art all I want;
More than all in thee I find;
Raise the fallen, cheer the faint,
Heal the sick, and lead the blind.
Just and holy is Thy name,
I am all unrighteousness;
False, and full of sin, I am,
Thou art full of truth and grace.
3 – Jesus, Lover of My Soul
Words: Charles Wesley
Music: Joseph P. Holbrook
© 2005 The Paperless Hymnal™

3 – Jesus, Lover of My Soul
© 2005 The Paperless Hymnal™

4.
Plenteous grace with Thee is found,
Grace to pardon all my sin;
Let the healing streams abound;
Make and keep me pure within.
Thou of life the fountain art,
Freely let me take of Thee;
Spring Thou up within my heart,
Rise to all eternity.
4 – Jesus, Lover of My Soul
Words: Charles Wesley
Music: Joseph P. Holbrook
© 2005 The Paperless Hymnal™

4 – Jesus, Lover of My Soul
© 2005 The Paperless Hymnal™

title: Joyful Joyful
slides:
1.
Joyful, joyful, we adore Thee,
God of glory, Lord of love;
Hearts unfold like flowers before Thee,
Opening to the sun above,
Melt the clouds of sin and sadness;
Drive the dark of doubt away;
Giver of immortal gladness,
Fill us with the light of day!
1 - Joyful, Joyful We Adore Thee
Words by: Henry van Dyke
Music by: Ludwig van Beethoven, Arranged by: Edward Hodges
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

1 - Joyful, Joyful We Adore Thee
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2.
All Thy works with joy surround Thee,
Earth and heaven reflect Thy rays,
Stars and angels sing around Thee,
Center of unbroken praise;
Field and forest, vale and mountain,
Flowery meadow, flashing sea,
Chanting bird and flowing fountain
Call us to rejoice in Thee.
2 - Joyful, Joyful We Adore Thee
Words by: Henry van Dyke
Music by: Ludwig van Beethoven, Arranged by: Edward Hodges
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2 - Joyful, Joyful We Adore Thee
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3.
Thou art giving and forgiving,
Ever blessing, ever blest,
Wellspring of the joy of living,
Ocean depth of happy rest!
Thou our father, Christ our Brother,
All who live in love are Thine;
Teach us how to love each other,
Lift us to the joy divine.
3 - Joyful, Joyful We Adore Thee
Words by: Henry van Dyke
Music by: Ludwig van Beethoven, Arranged by: Edward Hodges
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3 - Joyful, Joyful We Adore Thee
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4. Mortals join the mighty chorus,
Which the morning stars began;
Father love is reigning o'er us,
Brother love binds man to man.
Ever singing, march we onward,
Victors in the midst of strife;
Joyful music leads us sunward
In the triumph song of life.
4 - Joyful, Joyful We Adore Thee
Words by: Henry van Dyke
Music by: Ludwig van Beethoven, Arranged by: Edward Hodges
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4 - Joyful, Joyful We Adore Thee
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

1. O Little Town of Bethlehem,

amid the mystic shadows,

nature newly born;

in breathless adoration,

of the morn.

title: The Churchs One Foundation Webb
slides:
1.
The Church's one foundation
Is Jesus Christ her Lord
She is His new creation
By water and the Word;
From heaven He came and sought her
To be His holy bride;
With His own blood He bought her,
And for her life He died.
1 – The Church’s One Foundation
Words by: S. J. Stone
Music by: G. J. Webb
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

1 – The Church’s One Foundation
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2.
Elect from every nation,
Yet one o'er all the earth;
Her charter of salvation:
One Lord, one faith, one birth;
One holy name she blesses,
Partakes one holy food,
And to one hope she presses
With every grace endued.
2 – The Church’s One Foundation
Words by: S. J. Stone
Music by: G. J. Webb
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

2 – The Church’s One Foundation
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3.
Though with a scornful wonder
We see her sore oppressed,
Her doctrine rent asunder,
By names and creeds distressed,
Yet saints their watch are keeping,
They cry: "How long, how long?"
And soon the night of weeping
Shall be the morn of song.
3 – The Church’s One Foundation
Words by: S. J. Stone
Music by: G. J. Webb
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

3 – The Church’s One Foundation
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4.
'Mid toil and tribulation, And tumult of her war,
She waits the consummation Of peace forever-more;
Till with the vision glorious, Her longing eyes are blest,
And the great church victorious Shall be the church at rest.
4 – The Church’s One Foundation
Words by: S. J. Stone
Music by: G. J. Webb
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

4 – The Church’s One Foundation
© 2001 The Paperless Hymnal™

title: The Star Spangled Banner
slides:
Oh, say, can you see, by the dawn's early light,
What so proudly we hailed at the twilight's last gleaming?
Whose broad stripes and bright stars, thro' the perilous fight,
O'er the ram-parts we watched, were so gallantly streaming?
And the rockets' red glare, the bombs bursting in air,
Gave proof thro' the night that our flag was still there.
Oh, say does that Star-Spangled Banner yet wave
O'er the land of the free, and the home of the brave?

Words by: Francis Scott Key
Music by: John Stafford Smith

Where the foe's haughty host in dread silence reposes,
What is that which the breeze, o'er the towering steep,
As it fitfully blows, half conceals, half discloses?
Now it catches the gleam of the morning's first beam,
In full glory reflected, now shines on the stream:
"Tis the Star-spangled Banner;
Oh, long may it wave
O'er the land of the free, and the home of the brave.
2 - The Star Spangled Banner
Words by: Francis Scott Key

That the havoc of war and the battle's confusion,
A home and a country should leave us no more?
Their blood has washed out their foul footsteps' pollution;
No refuge could save the hireling and slave
From the terror of flight or the gloom of the grave;
And the Star-spangled Banner in triumph doth wave
O'er the land of the free, and the home of the brave.
